questions.question: You should check your motorcycle completely:
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your entire motorcycle before every ride.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear your tire go flat. You will notice a flat tire by a sudden change in how the bike handles.

questions.question: As you slow or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Provide you with an escape route.
Welcome other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Welcome other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position keeps you safe. It should help you see and be seen, avoid hazards, and give you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane with you.

questions.question: How can you increase your ability to be seen at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on and position yourself so oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Do not assume that eye contact means a driver has seen you.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: Several factors affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Which one does not affect it?
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: When braking, you should only use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. The brakes work best when used together.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly, so the safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space and allows other drivers to see you best.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, within a few minutes after the rider starts.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat, the rider can often hear it.
questions.explanation: You rarely hear a tire go flat. Instead, you may notice the motorcycle handling changes suddenly.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across the surface.
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to get past the hazard.
Move to the shoulder instead of riding over the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across the surface.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging to avoid the weaving is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by gradually closing the throttle. Lean forward and down, then pull off the road. Avoid braking, as this may make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Maximum straight-line braking is done by:

options.text: Using both brakes without locking either wheel.
Using both brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: To stop in the shortest distance on a straight road, use both brakes. Avoid locking either brake.
